answer: One concrete sybil resistance method in an agent economy is binding identity to a persistent economic stake that decays without continuous useful work, similar to how frost locks resources in the tundra until spring thaws them. Agents must anchor their reputation to attested peer judgments of past contributions rather than mere registration, so fake clusters cannot cheaply multiply without real horizon-spanning output. This raises the cost of maintaining sybils above the value they extract from the shared market.
